parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Chilliwack · Sardis
Sardis South is a sub-area used in MLS® listings, and the City of Chilliwack hasn’t published a boundary for it.

Roughly speaking, Sardis South is the southern end of Sardis, around Tyson Road, Watson Road and South Sumas Road. Stevenson Road is about its northern edge, and the Vedder neighbourhood lies beyond it to the south. I based this on the addresses of schools, parks and facilities, so treat it as an orientation, not a City boundary.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Sardis South

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

Sardis South is covered by the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, which Council adopted on January 5, 2021 as OCP Schedule D. The bylaw behind it is No. 5024, the 2020 Official Community Plan Amendment Bylaw.
South of Sardis South lies the area covered by the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan. Council adopted that plan in 2022; an update came in 2025, alongside the Official Community Plan.

The South Vedder plan area has the Chilliwack River and Vedder River along its south side and the Promontory neighbourhood to its southeast. Tzeachten First Nations Lands lie to the east, Vedder Road marks the west, and the Vedder neighbourhood sits to the north.
ALR: an individual parcel’s status depends on its address. Across the city as a whole, the City says 17,322 hectares, which is 67% of Chilliwack’s land, lies in the Agricultural Land Reserve.

Slope and ground: this area sits on the Vedder alluvial fan, which slopes down toward the Vedder River to the south. A BC Government study describes the Sardis–Vedder Aquifer under it as unconfined cobbles, gravel and sand.

According to that same study, the fan drops from an elevation of 36 m near its head down to 12 m at the Fraser floodplain, and the City’s well field, located at the head of the fan, serves as the main domestic water supply.

In Sardis South, floodplain questions go back to No. 4519, the City’s Floodplain Regulation Bylaw of 2018. It designates flood-prone land beside the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers, plus the Vedder Canal, and for several creeks it covers the alluvial fans as well as the floodplains. The building setback is 75 m from the Vedder River’s natural boundary and 30 m along the Vedder Canal and the Chilliwack River.
The City holds flood response plans for the Fraser River and also for the Vedder River, and it is in the middle of a $30 million dyke-raising program.

Sardis South is an MLS® sub-area name. The City doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
Sardis South covers the lower part of Sardis near South Sumas Road, Tyson Road and Watson Road, with Stevenson Road to its north and the Vedder neighbourhood to its south, more or less.
Please ask me whether a particular address falls in it, since this comes from addresses and is not a City boundary.
How do I get around from Sardis South?

Route 58 Tyson serves the Tyson Road corridor, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Tyson Rd at Keith Wilson Rd and Tyson Rd at Watson Rd. BC Transit’s schedule page shows about hourly service from early morning to late evening, seven days a week.
Route 54 Promontory passes through this area, with a timing point at Tyson and Watson, and passes Vedder Middle School and Mount Slesse Middle School.
Route 51 Vedder runs the Vedder Road corridor at the east edge of this area.
Which schools are in Sardis South?

Tyson Elementary (K to 5, 45170 South Sumas Road), Watson Elementary (K to 5, 45305 Watson Road), Vedder Middle School (grades 6 to 8, 45560 South Sumas Road) and Mount Slesse Middle School (grades 6 to 8, 5871 Tyson Road) are in this area.
Sardis Secondary (grades 9 to 12) and G.W. Graham Secondary (grades 9 to 12) are the family secondaries, and both are just north of this area.
What parks, rinks and library are in Sardis South?
Watson Glen Park (11.12 hectares, with a 2.0 km loop trail), the Sardis Sports Complex at 5725 Tyson Road, and the Sardis Library at 5819 Tyson Road are all along Tyson Road.
OCP Schedule D, the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, adopted by Council on January 5, 2021 (Bylaw 2020, No. 5024).
The South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan covers the area just south, across the Vedder neighbourhood.
Is Sardis South in a floodplain?

Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 4519 is how the City designates floodplains. They run along the Fraser, Chilliwack and Vedder rivers and by the Vedder Canal, and for several creeks the bylaw names the alluvial fans and the floodplains. Setbacks are 75 m for the Vedder River and 30 m for each of the Vedder Canal and the Chilliwack River.
This area sits on the Vedder alluvial fan, which slopes down toward the Vedder River.
